title: Closed pushforward compares base-change ranges
statement: Let $p:X\to S$, $g:T\to S$ be scheme morphisms, $q\in\mathbb Z$, $\Lambda$ a commutative ring, $F$ a sheaf of $\Lambda$-modules on $T_{\mathrm{et}}$, and $x\in X$. Use the canonical source and target stalks $A(U),B(U)$, maps $b_U:A(U)\to B(U)$, and restrictions $r_\varphi$ of [def-sbc-canonical-base-change-stalk-transitions]. Let $f:T'\to T$, let $i:Z\to T'$ be a closed immersion, and let $\zeta\in B(T')$. Write $F'=f^*F$, $Y'=T'\times_S X$, with projections $e':Y'\to T'$ and $h':Y'\to X$. If $r_i(\zeta)\in\operatorname{im}(b_Z)$, then the image of $\zeta$ under the target-functor coefficient map induced by the unit $F'\to i_*i^*F'$ belongs to the stalkwise image of the degree-$q$ base-change map for the square $Y'$ and coefficient $i_*i^*F'$ [sbc-def-base-change-map].

proof.text: Direct image along a closed immersion is exact on etale module sheaves. This follows stalkwise: on the image, the stalk is the original stalk, and off the image it is zero. Consequently the higher direct image is just the ordinary closed pushforward placed in degree zero. The stalk comparison is the one of [lemma-openclosed-stalk-lowerstar].

Closed-immersion base change identifies the inverse image of the closed pushforward with the closed pushforward on Y. Stacks 0959 supplies this comparison, and 03QP supplies exactness. Composition of derived direct images identifies the two sides and the base-change map for coefficients i_* i^* F with those of the square over Z. The units and pasting compatibility identify the coefficient map with the target transition. These are the geometric comparison and coherence assertions to be formalized in this item.

Apply the source identification to a chosen preimage of the restricted class. Naturality of the base-change comparison and the inverse-image composition isomorphism identify its image with the coefficient-unit image of the original class. Thus it is a preimage as required. Empty Z and negative q are included.
